candidate.title: TruSeq™ RNA
candidate.scope: The single TruSeq RNA product-preparation outline in the assigned Illumina poster panel: total RNA undergoes poly(A) selection, fragmentation with random hexamer priming, and first- and second-strand synthesis, ending at RNA-derived double-stranded DNA fragments. This is a component-level depiction; no kit generation, strand-specific variant, sequencing-ready adapter structure, sequencing operation or complete experimental implementation is established. The several fragment icons depict a material population, with no alternative workflow or independent branch shown.

states.label: Total RNA
features: Input is labeled Total RNA and represented by one long purple strand.
The strand is labeled 5′ at the left and 3′ at the right; no specific terminal chemical groups are drawn.

evidence.locator: Upper input: purple 5′–3′ strand and Total RNA label

states.label: Poly(A)-selected RNA in the depicted capture association
features: A long purple RNA strand ends in an A tract aligned with a T tract beneath it.
The T tract is linked to a gray support-like icon; the depicted RNA is associated with that capture structure.
The polyA select label identifies enrichment for RNA bearing an accessible poly(A) tract; the panel does not establish the purity or completeness of selection.

evidence.locator: Selection row: long purple strand, AAAAA/TTTTT alignment, gray icon and polyA select label
Aligned A and T tracts at the right end of the selected RNA illustration
evidence.rationale: The selection caption together with the aligned A/T tracts supports interpreting this as poly(A)-dependent capture. The gray icon supports attachment, but does not identify a particular support material or surface chemistry.

states.label: Fragments of selected RNA associated with random hexamer primers
features: The formerly long purple RNA is represented by several shorter purple segments.
Short blue bars lie along the purple segments beside the Random hexamer caption; these are interpreted as associated primers.
These fragments have the history of poly(A) selection followed by fragmentation; selection of the parent RNA does not require every resulting fragment to retain its poly(A) tail.
No support attachment is drawn at this boundary; a separate release or transfer operation is not specified.

evidence.locator: Middle region: Fragment and Random hexamer labels with short purple segments and short blue bars
Arrow from selection row to the fragmented RNA/blue-bar intermediate, followed by the arrow toward strand synthesis
evidence.rationale: The Fragment caption identifies shortening of the selected RNA, while Random hexamer and the blue bars identify primers associated with those fragments for subsequent strand synthesis. Because fragmentation follows selection, the selection criterion applies to the parent RNA and need not remain on each fragment.

states.label: Double-stranded cDNA fragments derived from selected RNA
features: Final material is represented by multiple blue paired-line fragments of differing lengths.
The cDNA identity is inferred from the RNA input, random hexamer intermediate and First and second strand synthesis caption.
The physical sequence carrier at the depicted endpoint is double-stranded DNA representing portions of the selected RNA population.
No adapters, barcodes, strand-identifying modifications or sequencing reads are depicted.

evidence.locator: Bottom region: blue paired-line products and First and second strand synthesis label
Route from the fragmented RNA/random hexamer row through the downward arrow to the paired blue products
evidence.rationale: First- and second-strand synthesis starting from primed RNA explains the blue duplex products as double-stranded cDNA. The connected route makes them sequence representatives of fragments of the poly(A)-selected RNA, without establishing any downstream sequencing configuration.

operations.label: polyA select
operations.description: Total RNA is subjected to poly(A) selection. The output illustration shows RNA bearing an A tract associated with a complementary T tract attached to a gray support-like icon. The capture reagent is a component of this operation; it is not a second workflow. No separate rejected fraction is depicted.
operations.mechanism: The aligned A and T residues are interpreted as complementary tract pairing that mediates selection on the depicted support. The support composition and capture performance are not specified.
operations.information_effect: Selection enriches the represented population for poly(A)-bearing RNA. Downstream fragments therefore represent the selected population; this does not establish perfect biological specificity for a particular RNA class.

evidence.locator: Arrow below Total RNA leading to the A/T capture illustration labeled polyA select
polyA select caption and aligned AAAAA/TTTTT tracts touching the gray icon
evidence.rationale: The caption explicitly identifies selection; complementary A/T alignment provides the depicted basis for interpreting capture of poly(A)-bearing RNA. A capture cartoon does not measure its specificity or recovery.

operations.label: Fragment; Random hexamer
operations.description: Selected RNA is shortened into fragments and associated with random hexamer primers, yielding the illustrated short purple RNA segments with blue bars. The two source captions are retained in one local operation because the panel supplies one combined fragment/primer material boundary. Fragmentation chemistry, reagent-addition order within this block and transfer away from the capture support are not resolved into separate operations.
operations.mechanism: Fragmentation breaks the long RNA into shorter templates; the Random hexamer caption and blue bars are interpreted as primer association with those RNA templates. No specific fragmentation reagent is identified.
operations.information_effect: RNA sequence information is distributed across shorter templates. The drawing supports fragment representation and supplies priming sites for the following synthesis; it does not promise full-length transcript copies.

evidence.locator: Downward arrow from the selected RNA into the region labeled Fragment and Random hexamer
Purple fragments with short blue bars between the selection and synthesis arrows
evidence.rationale: The Fragment caption accounts for the change from one long RNA to shorter segments. Random hexamer next to the blue bars and the downstream synthesis step supports their role as primers. Grouping the captions preserves this shared material boundary without inventing an isolated unprimed intermediate.

operations.label: First and second strand synthesis
operations.description: The primed RNA-fragment intermediate is converted through the broadly depicted first- and second-strand synthesis block to blue double-stranded fragments. This is interpreted as production of double-stranded cDNA; the individual enzymatic steps and handling of the RNA template are not separately drawn.
operations.mechanism: RNA-templated first-strand synthesis followed by second-strand synthesis is the interpretation of the source caption and connected RNA-to-duplex route. No enzyme identities, strand-removal chemistry or strand-specific implementation are established.
operations.information_effect: The output DNA fragments carry sequence information from portions of poly(A)-selected RNA. The panel ends before a sequencing readout, so it establishes the origin of the sequence carrier but does not establish read structure, molecule counts, cell identity or strand-specific information.

evidence.locator: Arrow below the fragmented RNA/primer row and final paired blue products labeled First and second strand synthesis
First and second strand synthesis caption interpreted in the connected RNA-input workflow
evidence.rationale: The RNA templates and associated random hexamers precede the synthesis arrow, and paired blue strands follow it. Together these support RNA-to-double-stranded-cDNA conversion at schematic scope without resolving the internal chemistry of this broad block.

evidence.locator: Downward arrow from Total RNA to the polyA select row
polyA select label at the endpoint of the input arrow: RNA A tract associated with T tract and gray icon

method_scopes.rationale: The card and figure both identify only TruSeq RNA. All three local operation blocks belong to its single depicted route. No alternative target workflow is named. This assignment is to the literal poster depiction and does not generalize the route to every TruSeq RNA kit or version. The supplied card has an empty reference list and explicitly requires no primary-paper association; no publication match or historical claim is invented.

evidence.locator: Catalogue title and description_verbatim
TruSeq RNA title and entire single vertical workflow through First and second strand synthesis

checks.rationale: The independently inspected panel is fully represented by four material boundaries, three local operation blocks and six corresponding input/output connections. Its repeated fragment icons depict one population along one arrowed route, with no separate fraction, compartment, alternative or pooling interface. Combining Fragment and Random hexamer is appropriate because their shared intermediate is the only material boundary drawn; first- and second-strand synthesis likewise remains a broad source block. The candidate distinguishes visible symbols from its cDNA/capture interpretations, preserves selection limitations and the support association, and does not invent adapters, sequencing, enzymes, kit versions or complete implementation details. No source conflict requiring correction is evident. The supplied catalogue text only repeats the title; the card has references=[] and require_paper_matches=false. Accordingly, empty paper_matches, corrections and unknowns do not omit a required association or a consequential unresolved claim at this schematic scope. No primary-paper or full-text verification is claimed.

checks.rationale: Both card and image name TruSeq RNA as the sole target. All three assigned operations lie on its single depicted route and have compatible input histories.
